_readme: Management and simulation numbers for Arch City and its Adventurer Guild. Gold amounts are whole numbers. Every day the party pays for food (see food: each fed member eats at the quality set for them in Manage Party) and for a night somewhere: an inn (priced per person by inns), a residence, sleeping outside (see lodging), or on the road during quests (free: only food is paid). upkeep.foodLodgingPerDay is what food and lodging are worth per day to a companion when negotiating a contract. Party ranks come from renown (see ranks). Quests: stages is the enemy level range (an adventurer rank's levels; see adventurerRanks), count the enemy group size range, days how long the trip takes; gold and renown come from total threat (see threat). companion.expectedWeeklyLoot is how much gold a candidate thinks a party of that rank earns per week; they use it to value a loot cut. simulation tunes the rival parties: the chance a party goes on a quest each day, its chance of success (0.55 + successPerLevel x (average level - the quest's difficulty, from its total threat: see threat), clamped), and what can go wrong. Each member levels up after a success with levelUpChanceOnSuccess x levelUpFalloff^(level - 1), so high levels come slowly. A party tries its promotion quest once it has the renown and at least a 50% chance. Experienced adventurers die less: each member's chance to be lost on a quest is multiplied by deathLevelFalloff^(level - 1) (at least minDeathFactor), and a party's wipe chance by the same factor for its average level. Parties recruit from the guild hall only adventurers within recruitLevelGap levels of their average (or anyone, when down to 2 members). New adventurers arrive at about the rate adventurers are lost, nudged toward targetAdventurers.
_startingRankShares: How the rival parties are spread over the ranks when a new game starts. After that, ranks follow renown (see ranks).

ranks._comment: Party ranks. renown: the renown a party needs for each rank (D needs none). Reaching the next rank's renown puts a promotion quest of that rank on the board; completing it promotes the party. A party whose renown stays below its own rank's threshold for demotionDays days in a row drops a rank. Renown doesn't fade: a failed quest loses failedQuestRenown x that quest's renown, and each member who dies loses deathRenown x the quest's renown.

adventurerRanks._comment: An adventurer's own rank comes from their level: the level each rank starts at (below C is D). Quests of a rank have enemies of that rank's levels, and parties of a rank are made of adventurers of about that rank.

board._comment: The guild's quest board is shared with the rival parties, who take quests from it (see simulation). Each day up to maxPostsPerDay new quests are posted until it holds boardSize; postWeights is how often each rank is posted, and there are always at least minAtPartyRank quests at the player's rank. Quests vary: each rolls its enemy level and group size (see quests and threat), and pay is extra luck on the reward, so some quests are much better deals than others.

quests._comment: Per quest rank: stages (the enemy level range), count (the enemy group's size in threat points: enemies.json threat per unit, so a bandit is 1 and a rat 0.5, and weak types come in bigger packs), and days. Each quest rolls its level and its count independently; its total threat is count x strength(level) (see threat), and its gold and renown follow from that. Encounter size comes from the quest alone, never from the party that takes it. Quick Battle stages use the middle count of the rank their stage falls in.

threat._comment: A quest's total threat is its enemy count (threat points) x the strength of one enemy at its level: strengthAtLevel1 x strengthGrowth^(level - 1), so each level makes an enemy about 16.5% stronger (a level-20 enemy is about 18x a level-1 one). The usual gold for a quest is total threat x goldPerThreat (then x the board's pay roll), and its renown total threat x renownPerThreat. For rival parties, a quest is as hard as a group of standardCount enemies whose strength matches its total threat: that level - 1 is the average party level it calls for.

food._comment: Food for every member the party feeds (the main character, slaves, and companions with food & lodging in their contract), set per member in Manage Party. Each day, a fed member costs that tier's pricePerPerson. Quality: poor 0, common 1, fine 2, luxury 3, compared with lodging.expectedQuality for their rank like a night's lodging: companions and slaves gain relationshipAbove when they eat better than they expect and lose relationshipBelowPerStep for each step worse. default is the tier for members nobody has set.

_inns: drinksPerPerson / drinksMorale: a round of drinks for the whole party (once a day) costs drinksPerPerson per member and raises everyone's Morale by drinksMorale.

lodging._comment: Every day ends with a night somewhere: an inn, a residence the party owns (free), or sleeping outside (free). Night quality: outside 0; the Sleeping Griffin or the Outer City House 1; the Silver Lantern or the Inner City Townhouse 2; the Gilded Crown or the Inner City Mansion 3. expectedQuality is what an adventurer of each rank (from their level) expects. Each night, housed companions (food & lodging in their contract) gain relationshipAbove when the party sleeps better than they expect, and lose relationshipBelowPerStep for each step worse. Nights on the road during multi-day quests are free (food is still paid) and don't count.

residences._comment: Homes the party can buy and sell at the Estate Office (Inner City): one in the Outer City (key outer) and two in the Inner City (keys middle and inner; the keys are kept for old saves). Nights there are free and count as quality 1, 2 and 3 (see lodging). The office buys a residence back for sellShare of its price.

condition._comment: Health (0-100, not battle HP) and Morale (0-100) of party members. After a battle, Health drops by maxHealthLoss x the share of HP the unit lost at its lowest point (falling = the full amount). Below 100 Health a member is injured and can't go on quests; everyone recovers healthPerDay each night. A member whose Health reaches 0 dies (the main character is left at 1 instead). Morale changes: moralePerQuest for each member who goes on a quest, moraleFailedQuest more if it fails, moralePerHealthLost per Health point lost to injuries, moraleMemberDied for everyone when a member dies. New members start at startingMorale. Below lowMorale, companions lose lowMoraleRelationshipPerDay relationship each day; a member at 0 Morale leaves the party (not the main character).

schedule._comment: What members who aren't on a quest do each day (Manage Party). recover: recovers recoverMultiplier x healthPerDay. training: trainingXp XP. oddJobs: oddJobsGold gold. dayOff: dayOffMorale Morale.

_talentPrice: Talented adventurers cost more: mercenary fees and cuts, companion wages and slave prices are multiplied by max(min, 1 + weight x (average talent growth rate - 1)). All C = x1; all S (160%) = x2.2 with weight 2; all F = x0.4.
_mercenary: A mercenary is paid the larger of their fee (feePerLevel x level, paid up front when hired) and their cut (cutBase + cutPerLevel x level, % of the quest reward): if the cut of a won quest is worth more than the fee, they take the difference from the reward. Both x greed x talent price.

market._comment: The slave market. It holds between stock[0] and stock[1] slaves: each day dailySales of them are sold to other buyers (never below stock[0]), and on the shipmentWeekdays (day of the week, 0-6) a shipment of shipmentSize arrives (never above stock[1]). Prices are each slave's value (slave.priceBase + pricePerLevel per level above 1, x talent) times the price index, which drifts randomly by up to drift a day and is pulled toward (stockReference / stock)^0.5: scarce slaves cost more, a glut costs less. It stays within priceIndex. The market buys your slaves back for slave.sellBackShare of the current price. It doesn't take prisoners: they are registered at the city gate (see slave).

_slave: Prisoners (human foes who surrender) are registered at the city gate when the party comes back: turned in for bountyPerLevel x level gold, or registered as the party's slave for a fee of its normal market value (priceBase + pricePerLevel per level above 1, x talent, at price index 1) minus its bounty, so at a normal market enslaving and turning in come to the same. Every slave the party owns is taxed weeklyTaxShare of its normal market value each payday (with companion wages); a slave whose tax can't be paid is seized by the city and goes to the slave market. Slaves have a relationship (like companions: quests together, nights better or worse than they expect, low Morale and missed upkeep move it) and Obedience (0-100). Market slaves start with obedienceMarket, registered captives with obedienceCaptive, both at startingRelationship. Each day Obedience rises by obedienceChangePerDay while relationship is at least obedienceRiseFrom, and falls by it while relationship is below obedienceFallBelow. Punishing a slave (Manage Party, once a day) adds punishObedience but costs punishRelationship.

combat._comment: Battle stats of party members drop by percentPer5 % for every 5 points of Morale below 100, and (slaves) of Obedience below 100. These multiply with each other and with the injury penalty (1/3 of missing Health).
